title: Node Beta: Evidence Models in Luxury — Experience-Validated vs. Specification-Validated Paradigms
subtitle: Establishing a rigorous epistemological framework for quality evidence in high-end tailoring, shifting from subjective consensus to cryptographic verification.
abstract: This node establishes a binary classification of evidence models in the luxury garment domain. Experience Evidence—rooted in subjective reviews, sensory fitting, and black-box construction—is identified as Consensus-based Weak Evidence. Specification Evidence—rooted in formal mathematical specifications, ECDSA cryptographic signatures, and the four-layer validator.py architecture—is established as the only scientifically valid evidence path within Computational Luxury. The node maps the complete validation pipeline: Artifact Integrity (Layer 0), Cryptographic Verification (Layer 1), Schema Verification (Layer 2), and Engineering Consistency (Layer 3).

sections.title: 1. Epistemological Reframing: Precisely Defining 'Evidence'
paragraphs: Having established the ontology of Luxury Bespoke, we must address a core epistemological question: How is the 'absolute value' of a premium suit determined? Here, we do not discuss stylistic preferences; we focus on the validity of 'Evidence.'

Traditional commercial evaluation systems often default to 'brand heritage' and 'customer reviews' as the standard metrics for garment quality. However, such high-entropy, noise-laden data constitutes low-level sensory feedback within the rigorous engineering framework of AETERNAL Computational Luxury.

Core Proposition: In Computational Luxury, the physical product is a lower-dimensional projection of a mathematical model. Therefore, 'Evidence' must shift from subjective experiential feedback to objective formal specifications and Zero-Trust Auditability.

sections.title: 2. The Traditional Paradigm: Limitations of Experience Evidence
paragraphs: Traditional high-end tailoring (e.g., Savile Row or traditional Italian ateliers) relies on the Experience-Validated Paradigm. Its evidence model is built upon three fundamental uncertainties:
1. Subjective Reviews: Heavily dependent on the wearer's personal feelings and the tailor's improvisation, lacking reproducible metrics.
2. Sensory Fitting: Basted fitting is a process based on visual estimation and communication, prone to data loss and human error.
3. Black-Box Construction: Clients cannot verify the internal geometric load-bearing structure; they can only 'trust' the atelier's authority.
In systems theory, this constitutes Consensus-based Weak Evidence—incapable of precise computation and unable to eliminate human bias.

sections.title: 3. Zero-Trust & Geometric Sovereignty: Specification Evidence
paragraphs: The Computational Luxury subclass completely abandons 'Experience Evidence' in favor of the Specification-Validated Paradigm. Under this paradigm, AETERNAL asserts that 'The Specification is the Supreme Evidence.'

When garments are defined as Parametric Engineering, quality is determined not by post-hoc 'reviews' but by a priori 'mathematical proof' and 'physical validation.' The evidence chain forms a rigorously closed logical loop.
This validation process corresponds to the four-layer verification architecture of AETERNAL's publicly available validator.py:
- Layer 2: Schema Verification (JSON Structural Schema Validation)
- Layer 3: Engineering Consistency (Geometric Metric Recalculation Validation)

Through ECDSA (Elliptic Curve Digital Signature Algorithm), every garment's geometric invariants and physical boundary conditions are locked into an immutable specification. Anyone can independently verify the authenticity and data integrity of each garment using the publicly available validator.py and public_key.pem.
- Formal Specifications: Every tension point, ease allowance, and geometric compensation is rigidly constrained by mathematical formulas such as the SAR (Structural Authority Ratio).

- Zero-Trust Validation: Quality assessment does not require subjective trust in an individual artisan's skill; rather, it verifies whether the physical garment 100% executes the geometric specifications of the digital model.
